title: Île-de-France
credit_line: Maurice Wertheim Collection; exact object credit wording unverified
identity_evidence: Polytech capture title names Maillol, 1925, bronze; public capture GPS locates Harvard Art Museums. Harvard Magazine’s 2001 photograph identifies Île de France at Fogg among the Maurice Wertheim collection. A 2017 visitor transcription of the gallery label and 2014 visitor photograph corroborate this cast. Accession, foundry, cast date and dimensions intentionally omitted.
rights_assessment: Public-domain assessment: Maillol died in 1944, and the ordinary French 70-year term expired in 2015. Orsay documentation records the full ensemble at the Salon d’Automne in 1930, before the current U.S. 1931 publication threshold. Do not apply this reasoning to the late 1930s River/Air compositions. This model is Polytech’s independently made public/savable CC BY 4.0 capture; no Harvard image is republished.
attribution: Île-de-France, Aristide Maillol, 1925 (composition; cast date unverified), bronze. Scanned at Harvard Art Museums / Fogg Museum. 3D scan by Polytech via Polycam, CC BY 4.0. Atrium repackaged the glTF as GLB; source geometry and textures unchanged.
curatorial_note: A cloth held behind the hips draws the shoulders back, opening the figure’s chest and creating a gentle arc through the body.
